q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Circular journey tickets are issued for round tours which begin and end at the same station, the outward and return journeys being performed by different routes.
2. A passenger travelling on a Circular Journey Ticket is entitled to break his journey at intermediate stations on the route, subject to the prescribed conditions and endorsement.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Concessional season tickets for students are issued for travel between the student's residence and the educational institution attended by him.
2. Students travelling in a group on an educational tour sponsored by a recognised educational institution are entitled to concession in rail fares, on production of the prescribed concession certificate or form from the institution.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
A patient seeks concession in rail fare for travelling in connection with medical treatment. Under the prescribed conditions, such concession for medical treatment is admissible to:

options.A: All patients suffering from any ailment whatsoever
options.B: Thalassemia major and haemophilia patients travelling for treatment or periodic check-up
options.C: Only patients referred by a Government hospital
options.D: Only children below twelve years of age

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Concession in rail fares is admissible to Divyangjan passengers, such as the orthopaedically handicapped and the visually impaired, on production of the prescribed certificate.
2. The concession in fare admissible to such Divyangjan passengers is available in all classes, including the air-conditioned classes.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
A passenger is granted a concession in fare admissible under the rules. The concession so granted is calculated:

options.A: On the total fare including all supplementary charges
options.B: On the reservation charge and the superfast charge only
options.C: On the Tatkal charges, where the ticket is booked under the Tatkal scheme
options.D: On the basic fare only, the other charges being payable in full

q: A contractor is awarded a parking contract at a station and, as the successful tenderer, deposits earnest money for the contract. The earnest money so deposited is:

options.A: Adjusted towards, or retained as, security for the due performance of the contract
options.B: Forfeited to the Railways in all cases
options.C: Refunded to him on the very day the contract is awarded
options.D: Treated as a traffic earning of the station

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The rules governing the booking and carriage of explosives and other dangerous goods on the Railways are contained in the Red Tariff.
2. Before explosives and other dangerous goods are accepted for carriage, they are required to be declared by the consignor and packed and labelled in accordance with the Red Tariff Rules.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

A consignment is misdespatched because its packages bore nothing by which they could be identified. To prevent such misdespatch and loss, the Goods Tariff requires every package of a consignment to carry:

options.A: The seal of the forwarding station
options.B: The value of the contents of the package
options.C: Distinct identification marks and the name of the destination station
options.D: The telephone number of the consignor

q: A consignor furnishes a wrong description of goods in the Forwarding Note and the Railways suffer loss on that account. In regard to responsibility for the particulars and for the loss, the correct position is that:

options.A: The Railways alone bear the loss, as the particulars are accepted as declared
options.B: The destination station bears the loss in all such cases
options.C: The consignor bears no responsibility once the Railway Receipt is issued
options.D: The consignor is responsible for the correctness of the particulars furnished by him, and the loss suffered by the Railways on account of incorrect particulars is recoverable from him

q: At a goods shed, a merchant books a consignment in his own name as both the consignor and the consignee. In goods traffic, such a consignment is said to be booked to:

Consider the following statements:
1. The Traffic Accounts Office of a zonal railway functions under the overall control of the Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer of the railway.
2. The Traffic Book of a zonal railway, showing the earnings of local and through traffic, is compiled in the Traffic Accounts Office of the railway.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Passenger fares and freight rates on Indian Railways are fixed by the Railway Board (Ministry of Railways).
2. The classification of commodities for the purpose of goods freight rating is issued by the Indian Railway Conference Association.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
A branch line which is uneconomic is retained in operation at the request of a State Government. The losses on such a line are:

options.A: Borne wholly by the Railways in all cases
options.B: Recovered from the passengers travelling on the line
options.C: Written off against the sundry other earnings of the railway
options.D: Shared with the State Government at whose request the line is retained

q: A newly posted accounts clerk has to consult the code provisions dealing with station accounts, traffic earnings and traffic statistics. The volume he should refer to is:

Consider the following statements:
1. Credits for remittances deposited by stations at the focal point branches of the bank are afforded in the Cash Office on the basis of the scrolls and returns of remittances received from the bank.
2. Under the door-step banking arrangement for station earnings, the station cash is collected from the station by the authorised bank and deposited directly into the Railways' bank account.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Unauthorised carrying on of the business of procuring and supplying railway tickets (touting) is punishable under Section 143 of the Railways Act, 1989.
2. Trespass upon railway premises, and refusal to leave the premises when requested to do so, is punishable under Section 147 of the Railways Act, 1989.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. 'Rail Madad' is the facility provided by Indian Railways for registration, tracking and resolution of passenger complaints and grievances through a single integrated platform.
2. The integrated helpline number of Indian Railways for passenger enquiries, assistance and Rail Madad services is 139.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
In the Freight Operations Information System, the module which deals with the formation, placement, movement and release of freight rakes is the:
Locomotives on a railway are fitted with a system which automatically transmits their location and movement in real time. This system is the:

At the close of the day, a booking clerk records the day's coaching earnings and the particulars of the tickets issued by the station in the prescribed daily record maintained for the purpose. This record is the:
An agency at a place not served by rail, linked to a railhead station, for booking and delivery of traffic, is known on the Railways as:

Consider the following statements:
1. In connection with coaching operations, the abbreviation COIS stands for Coaching Operations Information System.
2. In connection with coaching operations, the abbreviation ICMS stands for Integrated Coaching Management System.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. In container traffic, TEU stands for Twenty-foot Equivalent Unit.
2. One Forty-foot Equivalent Unit (FEU) in container traffic is equal to two TEUs.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
A small station has no regular booking staff of its own, and unreserved tickets there are issued at the station itself by an agent engaged on a commission basis. Such an agent is known as a:

Consider the following statements:
1. A Railway Receipt is a document of title to the goods, transferable by endorsement and delivery.
2. A Railway Receipt is a negotiable instrument.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
The fare computed for a passenger journey works out to an amount which is not a multiple of five rupees. In such a case, the fare charged from the passenger is:

options.A: The computed amount itself, without any rounding
options.B: Rounded off to the next higher multiple of five rupees
options.C: Rounded off to the next lower multiple of five rupees
options.D: Rounded off to the nearest multiple of ten rupees

q: Loaded trucks of a road transporter are placed on flat wagons and carried by rail over a long lead, the trucks being unloaded at the destination and driven away with their loads. This service of the Railways is known as:
A parcel is booked for carriage by a Rajdhani Express train. The parcel charges on it are levied under:

options.D: The goods tariff scale for smalls

q: A wagon placed for loading is loaded by the consignor himself. In such a case, the correct position is that:

options.A: The Railways count and verify the contents of the wagon before the Railway Receipt is issued
options.B: No Railway Receipt is issued for such a wagon
options.C: The freight on the wagon is charged at the railway risk rate in all cases
options.D: The Railway Receipt bears an endorsement that the wagon was loaded by the consignor, and the Railways do not verify the count or contents at the time of loading

q: During a month, a station has paid out refunds of fares and freight under proper sanction. When the station's accounts are received in the Traffic Accounts Office, these refunds are:

options.A: Treated as final and are not subjected to any check
options.B: Checked against the refund statements and records rendered by the stations
options.C: Debited in full to the station staff who paid them
options.D: Adjusted against the sundry other earnings of the station

q: In respect of container trains run by licensed private container train operators, the correct position is that:

options.A: The freight rates for their customers are fixed by the Railway Board
options.B: The operators carry the containers free of any charge for the use of the railway network
options.C: The operators fix their own commercial rates for their customers and pay haulage charges to the Railways for the use of the railway network
options.D: The operators are required to hand over their rakes to the Railways after every trip

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The official mobile application of IRCTC for booking reserved e-tickets is 'IRCTC Rail Connect'.
2. The in-built wallet facility provided in the 'UTS on Mobile' application of Indian Railways is known as R-Wallet.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

An officer wants to consult the published annual summary of Indian Railways' performance, covering their earnings, traffic and statistics. This publication, the 'Year Book' of Indian Railways, is brought out by:

options.A: The Centre for Railway Information Systems

q: Overloading of wagons in a goods train is detected without stopping the train, the wagons being weighed while in motion en route. This is done with the help of:

options.A: The weighbridge installed in the goods shed
options.C: The crane provided at the loading point
options.D: The re-weighment facility at the destination station

q: A dispute arises about the terms on which a private siding is to be worked, the charges leviable and the responsibility for its maintenance. These terms are laid down in:

options.A: The practice followed at the serving station
options.B: The orders of the Railway Claims Tribunal
options.C: The agreement executed between the Railways and the siding owner
options.D: The agreement executed between the siding owner and the State Government

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Newspapers and magazines offered for carriage by passenger trains are treated on the Railways as parcel traffic, booked on parcel way bills and charged at the parcel scales.
2. Registered newspapers and periodicals offered for carriage by passenger trains are charged at concessional parcel rates.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. A platform ticket is valid for two hours from the time of its issue.
2. A paperless platform ticket can be booked by a passenger through the UTS mobile application.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. In many long-distance trains, a separate quota of reserved accommodation is earmarked for allotment to foreign tourists holding a valid passport and visa.
2. Reserved accommodation under the Foreign Tourist Quota can be booked by foreign tourists up to 365 days in advance of the journey.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
During a surprise check of a station, a shortage of cash is found as compared with the balance shown in the station accounts. The shortage is:

options.A: Written off at the station itself at the close of the month
options.B: Adjusted against the excess cash found at other stations of the division
options.C: Debited to the station and recovered from the staff responsible for it
options.D: Treated as a traffic earning of the station

q: The Gross Tonne Kilometres performed on a railway during a period are 1,56,00,000 and the goods train kilometres run are 40,000. The average gross load of goods trains is:
Coal moves from a colliery to the thermal power plant linked to it in dedicated rakes which shuttle continuously between the two points. This system of working is known as:
A manufacturer despatches motor cars by rail in specially modified wagons designed for the carriage of automobiles. These wagons are known as:

Under a scheme of the Railways, stalls and outlets at stations are allotted for the display and sale of the local and indigenous products of the region in which the station is situated. The scheme is:
At the zonal and divisional levels, the Railways have set up units whose primary job is to tap new streams of freight traffic and to maintain liaison with trade and industry. These units are the:

Consider the following statements:
1. In parcel traffic, the parcel charges are required to be prepaid at the time of booking.
2. Freight charges on consignments of a perishable nature are required to be prepaid at the time of booking.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
A consignor offers explosives for carriage and asks that they be sent by the next passenger train. The correct position is that explosives are accepted for carriage:

options.A: By any train, including passenger trains, without any special condition
options.B: Only in the brake van of passenger trains
options.C: Only against a cash deposit equal to the value of the explosives
options.D: Only by goods trains, subject to the conditions laid down in the Red Tariff

q: In the normal monthly cycle of internal check of station accounts, the Advice of Internal Check reaches a station:

options.A: Only when an error is detected in its accounts
options.B: Every month, after the check of the station's monthly balance sheet and returns
options.C: Once a year, at the close of the financial year
options.D: Only on the demand of the station concerned

q: The Reserve Bank of India tenders currency notes for carriage by rail from one centre to another. Such treasure consignments are carried by the Railways:

options.A: In ordinary goods wagons along with other traffic
options.B: Only by road, the Railways not accepting such consignments
options.C: In special treasure vans or coaches, under proper escort and on payment of the prescribed charges
options.D: Free of charge, as Government traffic

q: The free time allowed for the loading or unloading of a wagon is reckoned from:

options.A: The time the wagon is placed at the loading or unloading point for that purpose
options.B: The time the train carrying the wagon arrives in the station yard
options.C: The time the indent for the wagon was registered by the consignor
options.D: The midnight following the arrival of the wagon at the station

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Parcels which are not taken delivery of by the consignees within the free time allowed after their arrival at the destination station are liable to wharfage charges for the period for which they remain on the station premises.
2. Charges for depositing luggage in the cloak room at a station are levied per package, for each period of 24 hours or part thereof.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
Under a scheme of the Railways, bulk consumers and industries could own wagons, which were operated by the Railways, so as to ensure assured supply of wagons for their traffic. The scheme was the:
A passenger booking an e-ticket opts for the travel insurance facility offered along with the booking. Subject to the terms of the policy, this insurance primarily covers:

options.A: Loss of the passenger's unbooked luggage during the journey
options.B: The cancellation charges deducted on cancellation of the ticket
options.C: Accidental death of, or injury to, the passenger during the course of the journey
options.D: Delay in the running of the train by which the passenger travels

q: Before a commodity offered for booking as goods traffic is accepted for carriage, the station must see that it complies with:

options.A: The packing conditions prescribed by the consignor himself
options.B: No packing conditions, the Railways accepting it as presented
options.C: The standard packing conditions prescribed for it in the Coaching Tariff
options.D: The standard packing conditions prescribed for it in the Goods Tariff

q: The goods earnings of a railway for a period are Rs 84,00,000 and the goods train kilometres run during the period are 1,20,000. The earnings per goods train kilometre are:
An e-ticket is partially confirmed and in Reservation Against Cancellation (RAC) after preparation of the reservation chart. In regard to such a ticket, the correct position is that:

options.A: It is cancelled automatically and no passenger named on it can travel
options.B: Only the confirmed passengers named on it can travel, the others being treated as ticketless
options.C: It is not cancelled automatically and the waitlisted passengers named on it may also travel
options.D: The fare of all the passengers named on it is refunded in full

q: At the close of March, a station has rendered services earning Rs 12 lakh for the month, but Rs 2 lakh of it, being 'to-pay' freight on goods delivered, is still to be received from the parties. A newly posted clerk asks what the full Rs 12 lakh figure in the accounts represents. The correct answer is that it represents the:

options.A: Earnings of the station, being the amounts that have accrued for the services rendered during the month, whether actually received or not
options.B: Revenue of the station, being the amount actually received by it during the month
options.C: Cash-in-transit of the station for the month
options.D: Sundry other earnings of the station for the month

q: A station accountant is closing the monthly Station Balance Sheet. The opening outstanding balance of the month was Rs 2,40,000, the earnings and other debits of the month were Rs 9,60,000, and the remittances and other credits of the month were Rs 10,50,000. The closing outstanding balance of the month works out to:

The Freight Operations Information System fails at a goods station and remains unavailable for several hours, during which customers are waiting with consignments for booking. The correct course for the station is to:

options.A: Refuse all goods booking until the system is restored, as manual booking is not permitted
options.B: Divert all the customers to the nearest station where the system is working
options.C: Book the goods manually and treat the transactions as closed, without entering them in the system later
options.D: Book the goods manually under the prescribed contingency arrangements, and feed the particulars of the consignments so booked into the system when it is restored, so that the traffic is duly accounted for

q: A divisional officer proposes two entries for the Traffic Suspense account of his railway: (1) the pay and allowances due to the station staff, and (2) the charges for traffic booked on credit notes and warrants for Government departments, pending recovery from those departments. Which of the proposed entries is/are correct?

After his inspection of a station, a Travelling Inspector of Accounts is asked by the station master to also prepare the Advice of Internal Check for the station, since he has just examined its accounts. The correct position in this regard is that:

options.A: The Travelling Inspector of Accounts is a field functionary of the Accounts Department who inspects stations, and the Advice of Internal Check is not prepared by him
options.B: The Travelling Inspector of Accounts prepares the Advice of Internal Check after every inspection of a station
options.C: The Advice of Internal Check is prepared jointly by the Travelling Inspector of Accounts and the station master
options.D: The Travelling Inspector of Accounts neither inspects stations nor has any connection with their accounts

q: For the same month, a station receives two communications from the Traffic Accounts Office: one gives the net debit to be taken to account for the month as a whole, and the other lists each individual error found in its returns, calling for its explanation and compliance. These two communications are, respectively, the:

options.A: Error sheet and the Advice of Internal Check
options.B: Station Balance Sheet and the error sheet
options.C: Advice of Internal Check and the error sheet
options.D: Accounts Office Balance Sheet and the Advice of Internal Check

q: A station clerk, finding certain suspense items in the station accounts still uncleared at the close of the financial year, proposes to write them off at the station itself so that the new year can begin with a clean slate. The correct position is that:

options.A: The station can write off such items on its own authority at the close of the year
options.B: Such items are automatically extinguished at the close of the financial year
options.C: Such items remain under watch until they are cleared with supporting particulars in the subsequent accounts, and cannot be written off by the station itself
options.D: Such items are transferred to the personal account of the station master at the close of the year

q: A through consignment booked under a single Railway Receipt has to pass over a break-of-gauge point, where the goods must be unloaded from wagons of one gauge and loaded into wagons of another gauge before proceeding. The consignor asks who will bear the cost of this transhipment. The correct answer is that:

options.A: The cost is recovered from the consignor in addition to the freight
options.B: The cost is recovered from the consignee before delivery at destination
options.C: The cost is shared equally between the Railways and the consignor
options.D: The transhipment is arranged by the Railways as part of the through carriage, and its cost is borne by the Railways

q: On weighment en route, a wagon is found to have been loaded beyond its permissible carrying capacity, and the goods clerk has to raise the charges for the irregularity. Consider the following statements about the charges so raised: 1. Freight is charged on the weight found loaded in excess of the permissible carrying capacity of the wagon. 2. The amount so recovered on account of the overloading is credited to the goods earnings of the Railways. Which of the statements is/are correct?

Demurrage of a large amount has accrued against a trader at a goods station, and the station official who levied it offers to waive the whole amount himself to settle the matter. The correct position regarding waiver of demurrage and wharfage is that:

options.A: Powers to waive such charges are delegated in graded monetary slabs, so that larger amounts can be waived only by higher authorities
options.B: The official who levied the charge can waive it himself in all cases, whatever the amount
options.C: Demurrage and wharfage, once accrued, can never be waived by any authority
options.D: Waiver of such charges requires the prior approval of the Railway Claims Tribunal

q: A shipper asks the goods clerk to explain the break-up of the freight quoted for his consignment. The correct explanation is that the freight comprises:

options.A: Only the line-haul charges for the distance over which the goods are carried
options.B: Only the terminal charges for the services rendered at the two terminals
options.C: A flat shunting charge together with the wagon hire for the transit period
options.D: Terminal charges for the services rendered at the originating and destination terminals, such as handling and documentation, together with line-haul charges based on the distance over which the goods are carried

q: A zonal railway receives wagons owned by a neighbouring railway, and its operating staff propose that these wagons must be returned empty to the owning railway immediately, since only wagons owned by the railway itself may be loaded on its lines. The correct position is that:

options.A: The goods wagons of the zonal railways form a common pool and are freely interchanged among the railways for loading, so the wagons received may be loaded on the receiving railway
options.B: The proposal is correct, as each railway may load only its own wagons
options.C: The wagons received may be loaded only after purchase of the wagons from the owning railway
options.D: The wagons received must be detained until the owning railway sends its own loading programme

q: More than eight months after entrusting his goods to the Railways, a consignor prefers a claim for refund of an overcharge of freight detected by him. Under Section 106 of the Railways Act, 1989, the position regarding his claim is that it is:

options.A: In order, as such claims can be preferred at any time within three years
options.B: In order, as no time limit applies to claims for refund of overcharges
options.C: Time-barred, as such a claim must be preferred in writing within six months from the date of entrustment of the goods
options.D: Maintainable only before the High Court, because of the delay

q: A 'to-pay' consignment arrives at the destination station, and on re-check an undercharge in freight is detected before delivery. The correct course for the destination station is to:

options.A: Deliver the goods and treat the undercharge as a loss to the Railways
options.B: Recover the undercharge from the consignee before delivery of the goods
options.C: Return the consignment to the forwarding station at the consignor's cost
options.D: Debit the undercharge to the forwarding station master personally and deliver the goods

q: A merchant books coal in open wagons for carriage by rail. The freight on such bulk traffic loaded in open wagons is generally charged on the basis of:

options.A: The actual weight of the coal as declared by the merchant
options.B: A fixed charge per wagon, irrespective of the wagon used
options.C: The carrying capacity of the wagon used
options.D: The volumetric measurement of the coal loaded

q: A consignee, whose consignment has arrived, asks the destination station to remove his goods from the station premises at once, promising to pay the demurrage and wharfage due on the consignment on his next visit. The correct course for the station is to:

options.A: Allow the removal, treating the promise as sufficient security for the charges
options.B: Allow the removal and recover the charges from the forwarding station
options.C: Write off the charges, since the goods are being removed promptly
options.D: Require the demurrage and other charges due to be paid before the goods are delivered or removed from the station premises

q: The siding statement rendered by a station for a month is received in the Traffic Accounts Office. The statement shows, in respect of the sidings served by the station:

options.A: Only the number of railway staff deputed to work in the sidings
options.B: The wagons placed in and removed from the sidings and the siding charges recoverable
options.C: Only the value of the goods stored by the siding owners in their godowns
options.D: The maintenance expenditure incurred by the Railways inside the sidings

q: A consignment arrives at the station for which it was booked, and after its arrival the consignee books it afresh from that station to another station for onward carriage. In goods traffic, this fresh booking of the consignment from the destination station is known as:

A trader brings goods into a goods shed for booking, but the goods are not loaded and keep lying in the shed well beyond the free time allowed for their loading. The charge leviable by the Railways for the goods so kept in the shed is:

options.A: Demurrage, for detention of the goods in the shed
options.B: Stabling charges, for occupation of the shed premises
options.C: Wharfage, leviable also in respect of goods brought into a goods shed for booking but kept there beyond the free time allowed, without being loaded
options.D: Crane charges, for the space occupied by the goods

q: A passenger holds a confirmed reserved ticket for an air-conditioned class but, finding the coach crowded, travels by his own choice in a lower non-air-conditioned class of the same train, obtaining a certificate from the ticket checking staff for the class actually travelled. In regard to the difference of fare between the two classes, the correct position is that he is entitled to:

options.A: No refund of any kind in any circumstance
options.B: A refund of the difference of fare between the two classes, claimed on the basis of the certificate issued by the ticket checking staff
options.C: A refund of the full fare of the air-conditioned class ticket
options.D: A refund of the difference only if he had surrendered the ticket before the departure of the train

q: A passenger cancels a confirmed Tatkal ticket a few hours before the journey and demands a full refund of the fare at the counter. The correct position regarding refund on cancellation of a confirmed Tatkal ticket is that:

options.A: Full refund is admissible on payment of the prescribed cancellation charge
options.B: Half of the fare is refundable at the discretion of the station master
options.C: The refund is admissible only if another passenger is found for the berth
options.D: No refund is admissible, except in the circumstances specified in the refund rules, such as cancellation of the train itself

q: A passenger cancels his reserved ticket and is refunded the fare after the prescribed deduction, but he claims that the reservation charge collected with the ticket should also be returned to him. The correct position is that on cancellation of a reserved ticket, the reservation charge:

options.A: Is not refunded to the passenger
options.B: Is refunded at half the rate collected
options.C: Is refunded in full along with the fare
options.D: Is adjusted against the cancellation charge payable by him

q: A cultural organisation books a special train for its members on payment of charges at the Full Tariff Rate (FTR). The charges so recovered by the Railways for such special trains and reserved coaches form part of:

options.D: The earnings of the organisation hiring the train

q: A soldier travelling on duty, for whom no berth is otherwise available, asks about the accommodation specially earmarked in trains for defence personnel travelling on duty or on warrants. This earmarked accommodation is known as the:

A family is booking reserved tickets for a journey: one child is four years old, and another child is nine years old, for whom a separate berth is demanded. Consider the following statements about the fares chargeable for the two children: 1. The four-year-old, being below five years of age, is carried free of charge, no separate berth being provided for the child. 2. For the nine-year-old, full fare is chargeable, a separate berth having been demanded for the child. Which of the statements is/are correct?

A Divyangjan passenger, holding the prescribed certificate and travelling with an escort, asks whether the concession in fare admissible to him extends to the escort accompanying him. The correct position is that:

options.A: The concession is admissible to the Divyangjan passenger alone, and the escort must pay the full fare
options.B: An escort accompanying such a Divyangjan passenger is also eligible for concession in fare
options.C: The escort is eligible for concession only when travelling alone on the return journey
options.D: The escort is carried free of charge in all classes

q: A group of passengers holds a single e-ticket booked through the internet. During the journey, the ticket checking staff ask for identity proof. The requirement in this regard is met if:

options.A: Every passenger named on the ticket produces a separate original identity proof
options.B: The passenger who made the booking alone produces the bank card used for payment
options.C: Any one of the passengers on the ticket carries, during the journey, the prescribed proof of identity whose particulars were furnished at the time of booking
options.D: A photocopy of the identity proof of any one passenger is produced

q: A station has collected superfast charges from passengers travelling by a superfast train, and the accounts clerk has to classify the amount in the earnings of the Railways. The superfast charge so levied forms part of:

options.D: The miscellaneous receipts of the station, outside the traffic earnings

q: A statistics clerk has to report the track kilometres of a double-line section whose route length is 120 kilometres. Counting each running line separately, as track kilometres are counted, the track kilometres of the section are:

The statistical cell of a zonal railway has to compile the monthly statement dealing with goods train performance for submission to the Railway Board. The monthly statistical statement relating to goods train performance is:

A costing officer is verifying a loco shed's monthly return, which shows that the goods locomotives consumed 9,000 litres of diesel oil during the month while performing 18,00,000 Gross Tonne Kilometres. On verification, the Specific Fuel Consumption (SFC) of the railway for the month works out to:

At an occupancy review, a division reports that against 90,00,000 seat kilometres offered during the period, its coaching services actually performed 54,00,000 passenger kilometres. The load factor (occupation ratio) reported for the coaching services is:
The passenger earnings of a railway for a period are Rs 66,00,000 and the number of passengers carried during the period is 22,00,000. The earnings per passenger of the railway for the period are:

A wagon statistics return of a railway has to show the wagon fleet and the wagon days for the period. For statistical purposes, these wagon fleet and wagon-day figures of Indian Railways are expressed in terms of:

For a pricing decision, the traffic costing cell separates that part of the cost of a service which changes with the volume of traffic handled, leaving out the costs which remain unaffected by such changes. The cost so separated is known, in traffic costing, as the:
